text:
England cruise to ODI series win over Australia as Ben Duckett scores century and Sonny Baker takes four wickets
England beat Australia by 97 runs in Hobart for 2-1 ODI series win; teams meet in five T20 internationals, starting in Melbourne on Saturday (8.15am UK); 'Sandpapergate' storm rumbles on with Cameron Bancroft backing up Usman Khawaja's claims that every member of team aware of 2018 plot
Wednesday 18 November 2026 11:16, UK
England secured a come-from-behind ODI series win over Australia as Ben Duckett's century and Sonny Baker's new-ball wickets teed up a thumping 97-run victory in the Hobart decider.
Harry Brook's side had been bowled out for just 131 in Perth last Friday, leaving them 1-0 down in the three-match series. However, England bounced back impressively in Adelaide on Sunday with a 135-run victory, before producing another convincing performance at Ninja Stadium. Australia were dismissed for 231 while chasing 329, with Brook claiming the final wicket of tailender Spencer Johnson.
Wednesday's victory was England's first over Australia in Hobart and followed a similar pattern to their Adelaide success. A total in excess of 300, built around a century from an opening batter - Ben Duckett on this occasion, following Tom Banton's century in Adelaide - proved too much for the hosts, whose top order once again struggled and fell cheaply while attempting to drive.
After Duckett's 133, his seventh ODI ton and first outside England and Pakistan, helped propel his side from 195-5 to 328 all out in 48.3 overs, Australia plummeted to 5-2 and 34-3 in reply - Baker (4-45) nicking off Mitch Marsh (1) and Josh Inglis (14) with out-swingers.
Australia were eventually dismissed in 46.5 overs with Alex Carey (37) the fifth man to fall, run out after a dismal mix-up with Cameron Green, who later left the field bloodied after being cracked on the helmet by a searing bouncer from Gus Atkinson (1-44) and was replaced by concussion substitute Ollie Peake (5).
Just like in Adelaide, the margin of England's victory could have been even greater had they proved sharper in the field, with Baker shelling Matt Renshaw (55) on six running in from deep third, Brook grassing the same player on 54 at wide long-off during the batter's 74 run-partnership with Carey for the fourth wicket.
Banton also spilt Johnson (15) off part-time seamer Brook, two balls before Duckett claimed the winning catch at deep midwicket.
There was one distinct difference from Sunday's game, though, in that England made the maverick call to send Jofra Archer (7 off 7) out to bat at No 6, ahead of Will Jacks, who went on to crack a second successive ODI fifty, this one from 40 deliveries.
The teams will now meet in a five-match T20I series, starting in Melbourne on Saturday (8.15am UK), with England out to do a white-ball double and Australia keen for a victory to bring attention back to on-field matters following the latest 'Sandpapergate' claims.
While the final ODI in Tasmania was ongoing, Cameron Bancroft - the player caught applying sandpaper to the ball in Cape Town eight years ago - wrote an article in the West Australian newspaper backing up Usman Khawaja's allegations that every member of the side back then was aware of the ball tampering scheme.
Duckett century and Jacks' late rally rescue England before Australia crumble
This was not a great day for Australia.
It was not a perfect one for England, either, with the away side stuttering with the bat once a 74-run opening stand between Banton (44 off 35) and Duckett was snapped in the ninth as Marsh brilliantly caught the former running back from mid-off.
Part-time off-spinner Renshaw (3-51) starred with the ball in the absence of injured frontliner Adam Zampa (back spasms), firstly by bowling a charging Joe Root for 12 and having Jordan Cox stumped for the same score and then by ending Duckett's fine knock.
England captain Brook (17) fell cheaply for the third time in the series, after efforts of one and five in Perth and Adelaide respectively, as he skied left-arm spinner Cooper Connolly to deep midwicket, while Archer holed out leg-side off spinner Travis Head.
The visitors were tottering at five down for under 200 at the point of Archer's dismissal but Duckett, who reached three figures from 94 balls, and Jacks then combined for a sixth-wicket stand of 46 before Jacks added 41 with Sam Curran (14) once Duckett fell from a top-edged sweep and then stitched a further 36 runs with the tail.
Atkinson, whose six took England past 300, then continued his dominance of Travis Head (4) by removing the Australia opener for the third time on the trot in this series - Head slashing to Root at slip from the fourth delivery of the chase.
When Marsh and Inglis swiftly followed, the home team looked toast and although Renshaw, Carey, Connolly (29) and Jack Edwards (31) - the latter backing up his 4-31 with the ball - gave Australia a flicker of hope, England ran out handsome winners.
Left-arm spinner Liam Dawson (3-42) justified his selection ahead of leg-spinner Adil Rashid once again with the wickets of Renshaw (caught and bowled) and Connolly (castled).
Results/schedule for England's Australia tour
ODIs 3.30am UK time, with T20s 8.15am UK time
- First ODI: Australia won by seven wickets in Perth
- Second ODI: England won by 135 runs in Adelaide
- Third ODI: England won by 97 runs in Hobart
- First T20I: Saturday November 21 (Melbourne)
- Second T20I: Tuesday November 24 (Carrara)
- Third T20I: Friday November 27 (Brisbane)
- Fourth T20I: Sunday November 29 (Sydney)
- Fifth T20I: Wednesday December 2 (Canberra)
digest_he: נבחרת אנגליה רשמה מהפך מרשים והבטיחה ניצחון בסדרת משחקי האחד-יום מול אוסטרליה, לאחר גמר מוחץ בהובארט שהסתיים ביתרון של 97 ריצות. האנגלים התאוששו מהפסד בפתיחת הסדרה בזכות מאה נהדרת של בן דאקט שהובילה את האורחים לסך של 328 ריצות. בתגובה, ההתקפה האוסטרלית התקשתה מול יכולת מסירת הכדור של סוני בייקר, שקטף ארבע וויקטס, והמארחים לא הצליחו להדביק את הקצב למרות מאמצי שחקני התחתית. הצדדים יפגשו כעת לסדרת משחקי טיו-וי במועדים הקרובים, בעוד שערוריות עבר סביב שיוף כדורים ממשיכות לרחף סביב השחקנים האוסטרליים בתקשורת.
